1.explanation:
• lib/features/replace/BpmnReplace.js and ReplaceOptions.js define how BPMN element types are replaced (e.g. Call Activity → Sub-Process) but do not invoke a resize when converting into an expanded Sub-Process.
• lib/features/replace-preview/BpmnReplacePreview.js drives the live preview of replacement shapes but isn’t pulling in the expanded Sub-Process’s default width/height.
• lib/features/modeling/behavior/ToggleElementCollapseBehaviour.js governs the collapse/expand transition – it shrinks or grows collapsed Sub-Processes but isn’t triggered when replacing a Call Activity with an expanded Sub-Process.
• lib/features/auto-resize/BpmnAutoResizeProvider.js contains the logic for automatically resizing containers when their type or contents change. It should pick up the replacement of a Call Activity → expanded Sub-Process and apply the Sub-Process’s default dimensions, but currently does not.
• lib/features/popup-menu/ReplaceMenuProvider.js and lib/features/drilldown/SubprocessCompatibility.js control which replace options (collapsed/expanded Sub-Process, Event Sub-Process, Call Activity, etc.) appear in the wrench menu. They expose unsupported choices, and once expanded you lose the Call Activity option and can’t revert.

Together, these files coordinate replacement, resizing, and context-menu entries. Fixing the bug will involve: ensuring that a Call Activity → expanded Sub-Process replacement triggers the auto-resize with the correct default dimensions, and cleaning up the ReplaceMenuProvider/SubprocessCompatibility logic so only supported transitions are offered and reversible.
1.bug_scenario: When turning a Task into a Call Activity and then into an Expanded Sub-Process, the shape remains the size of a Call Activity (i.e. looks like a Task) instead of resizing to the default Expanded Sub-Process dimensions.  At the same time, the wrench (context-pad) shows inappropriate entries (collapsed sub-process, which isn’t even fully supported, and once expanded you can’t revert back to Call Activity), effectively landing you in a dead end.

2.explanation:
• ReplaceOptions.js defines the list of replacement types (Task→Call Activity→Sub-Process). It also carries the default width/height for each type. The missing size for expanded subprocess on a Call Activity→Sub-Process swap is the root cause of the non-resizing.

• BpmnReplace.js contains the core API that executes a replacement. It forwards replacement hints (including target type and size) to the modeling command but currently ignores or drops the new size when going from Call Activity to Sub-Process.

• ReplaceMenuProvider.js is in charge of building the wrench-menu entries from the replacement options. It is responsible for showing too many options (collapsed subprocess), and for hiding Call Activity when in expanded subprocess state.

• ReplaceElementBehaviour.js listens for the replacement command and applies both the semantic change and the graphical update. It should pick up the resize instructions from ReplaceOptions, but it doesn’t for this path.

• ResizeUtil.js contains the shared logic for calculating new bounds on element resize. When an element type changes, it computes the new dimensions. The subprocess-expanded path is missing in its mapping, so the shape never grows to the correct size.

Together, these files control the menu entries you see, the replacement operation itself, and the resizing of the shape. Fixing the size metadata in ReplaceOptions, ensuring BpmnReplace/BpmnReplaceBehaviour honor that size, and cleaning up ReplaceMenuProvider to hide unsupported collapsed subprocess will resolve the issue.
2.bug_scenario:
When you take a BPMN Task and turn it into a Call Activity (via the wrench icon), the wrench menu then shows two unexpected extra entries (“sub-process collapsed” and “sub-process expanded”). If you pick “sub-process expanded” the shape never resizes to the larger sub-process shape (it remains the size of a Call Activity), and once in that state you can no longer convert it back to a Call Activity.

In other words:
1. Create a Task
2. Convert it to Call Activity → shape resizes correctly
3. Wrench menu now also shows “collapsed sub-process” and “expanded sub-process” (even though collapsed subprocess isn’t supported)
4. Convert to Expanded Sub-Process → shape stays small
5. Wrench menu no longer offers Call Activity → you’re stuck
